column2: The Tourney of [tourney_host.Capital.GetName]

The heralds wait in the hall in their tabards, the pennants are sewn and the carpenters have begun on the stands. All that is left is to say how great a tourney it shall be. A local tourney for the knights of my own lands, a tourney for the whole dukedom, or a grand tourney to which every knight of the realm is bidden in the name of the Lady?
A tourney for the knights of my own lands
A tourney for the whole dukedom
A grand tourney for all the realm!
On second thought, no tourney this year
Knights and lords of your own lands and your liege's other vassals are invited. The lists open in 30 days.
The knights and lords of your dukedom are invited. The lists open in 30 days.
Every knight and lord of the realm is invited. The lists open in 30 days.

[Root.GetTitledFirstName] [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName], greetings.

In thirty days the lists will be raised beneath the walls of [From.Capital.GetName], where the knights of the neighbouring lands shall break lances for honour and for the Lady. Your name has been spoken in the hall. Will you ride?

[From.GetTitledName]

[Root.GetTitledFirstName] [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName], greetings.

In thirty days the best lances of the whole dukedom will meet at [From.Capital.GetName]. Only knights of proven skill and lords of good blood are asked. The champion shall name the Queen of Love and Beauty and ride home laden with gold. Will you ride?

[From.GetTitledName]

[Root.GetTitledFirstName] [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName], greetings.

By the grace of the Lady, a Grand Tourney shall be held at [From.Capital.GetName] in thirty days, and the finest knights of all the realm are bidden to it. Bards will sing of the champion for a generation. Will you ride?

[From.GetTitledName]
I will ride, for honour and the Lady!
Regretfully, I cannot come
Such games are beneath me
Do not trouble me with these little tourneys again
Do not trouble me with tourneys of this kind again
No more tourneys, ever!

[Root.GetTitledFirstName] [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName], greetings.

In thirty days the knights of the neighbourhood will joust beneath the walls of [From.Capital.GetName]. A seat in the stands is kept for you, with wine and a good view of the lists.

[From.GetTitledName]

[Root.GetTitledFirstName] [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName], greetings.

In thirty days the best lances of the dukedom will meet at [From.Capital.GetName]. A seat in the stands is kept for you among the great lords of the land.

[From.GetTitledName]

[Root.GetTitledFirstName] [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName], greetings.

In thirty days the Grand Tourney of [From.Capital.GetName] begins, and every lord of the realm is bidden to see it. Your pavilion is already being raised.

[From.GetTitledName]
I will come. It shall be a fine spectacle!
I have better things to do than watch jousting
The stands are full, the pavilions crowd the meadow and the peasants press against the fences to stare at their betters. The heralds stand ready to call the first names.
Let the lists be opened!
War calls me away. The tourney must wait
Word comes from [From.GetTitledName]: the tourney of [From.Capital.GetName] is called off. The pavilions are struck and the knights ride home with their lances unbroken.
A pity
[From.GetTitledName] is dead, and the tourney at [From.Capital.GetName] has died with [From.GetHerHim]. The pennants hang black and the knights ride home in silence.
May the Lady receive [From.GetHerHim]

The heralds have read out the names of the knights who will ride at [From.Capital.GetName]. Some have fallen in the qualifying runs and gone home, others have ridden in from the far corners of the land with no name but their shields. Tomorrow the first pairs will be called.
I shall see to my horse

The herald calls my name, and then the name of my opponent: [tourney_foe.GetTitledName]. Across the lists [tourney_foe.GetSheHe] waits on [tourney_foe.GetHerHis] destrier, lance upright, pennant fluttering. The crowd falls quiet.
Lower my lance and ride!
First, a prayer to the Lady
The Lady hears you. Her blessing will ride with you in your next tilt.
A heavy purse for [tourney_foe.GetHerHim] to fall...
[tourney_foe.GetFirstName] takes the gold and will fall at the first touch of your lance.
[tourney_foe.GetFirstName] throws the purse back at you and will remember the insult.
I yield. Let another ride in my place
Before the heralds call us, a servant of [From.GetTitledName] slips into my pavilion with a heavy purse. [From.GetSheHeCap] asks only that I fall at the first pass. Nobody need ever know.
Gold is gold. I shall fall
Tell your master to keep [From.GetHerHis] gold and look to [From.GetHerHis] seat!

We thunder down the lists. [tourney_tilt_loser.GetFirstName]'s lance glances off my shield while mine strikes true, and [tourney_tilt_loser.GetSheHe] goes over the back of [tourney_tilt_loser.GetHerHis] horse in a crash of steel. The stands roar my name.

My lance shatters on [tourney_tilt_loser.GetFirstName]'s breastplate and hurls [tourney_tilt_loser.GetHerHim] from the saddle. [tourney_tilt_loser.GetSheHeCap] lies still a long while before the squires get [tourney_tilt_loser.GetHerHim] up, bleeding, and lead [tourney_tilt_loser.GetHerHim] away.

There is a sound like a tree splitting. My lance takes [tourney_tilt_loser.GetFirstName] full on and [tourney_tilt_loser.GetSheHe] is thrown under the hooves of [tourney_tilt_loser.GetHerHis] own horse. When the surgeons are done with [tourney_tilt_loser.GetHerHim], [tourney_tilt_loser.GetSheHe] will never be whole again.

My lance finds the slit of [tourney_tilt_loser.GetFirstName]'s visor. The point goes in, the shaft breaks, and [tourney_tilt_loser.GetSheHe] slides from the saddle without a sound. By the time the heralds reach [tourney_tilt_loser.GetHerHim], [tourney_tilt_loser.GetSheHe] is dead. The crowd does not cheer.

[tourney_tilt_loser.GetFirstName] barely lowers [tourney_tilt_loser.GetHerHis] lance before my point touches [tourney_tilt_loser.GetHerHis] shield and over [tourney_tilt_loser.GetSheHe] goes, rolling neatly in the sand. The purse was well spent.
For the Lady!
The Lady keep [tourney_tilt_loser.GetHerHis] soul

[tourney_tilt_winner.GetFirstName]'s lance takes me square on the shield and the world turns over. I land in the sand with a crash and the stands roar for [tourney_tilt_winner.GetHerHim], not for me. My tourney is over.

[tourney_tilt_winner.GetFirstName]'s lance shatters on my breastplate and I am flung from the saddle. When I wake, the surgeons are cutting away my armour and there is a great deal of blood. My tourney is over.

I remember [tourney_tilt_winner.GetFirstName]'s lance coming at me, and then nothing but pain. My horse rolled on me. The surgeons did what they could, but I will carry this tourney with me for the rest of my days.
I let [tourney_tilt_winner.GetFirstName]'s lance touch my shield and tumble from the saddle as agreed. The fall hurts my pride more than my body, and the gold soothes both.
[tourney_tilt_winner.GetFirstName]'s lance found the slit of my visor. I should be dead. By the grace of something older than the Lady, I am not.
Next time...

Grim news from the lists: [tourney_tilt_loser.GetTitledName] was killed in [tourney_tilt_loser.GetHerHis] tilt against [tourney_tilt_winner.GetTitledName], a lance point through the visor. The heralds have covered the body with [tourney_tilt_loser.GetHerHis] own banner.

Grim news from the lists: [tourney_tilt_loser.GetTitledName] was thrown under [tourney_tilt_loser.GetHerHis] own horse in [tourney_tilt_loser.GetHerHis] tilt against [tourney_tilt_winner.GetTitledName]. The surgeons say [tourney_tilt_loser.GetSheHe] will live, but never whole.
Such is the price of glory
Spare me the rest of the butcher's bill

The last tilt is done and I am the only rider left in the saddle. [From.GetTitledName] sets the champion's wreath on my head while the crowd chants my name and the peasants at the fences cheer as if they knew it.

I am champion of the Grand Tourney of [From.Capital.GetName]! The finest knights of the realm have fallen before my lance one by one. [From.GetTitledName] sets the champion's wreath on my head, the trumpets sound, and the bards are already making a song of it.
Glory to the Lady!
In the final tilt [tourney_champion.GetTitledName] had the better of me, but no one else at [From.Capital.GetName] could unhorse me. Second place is no shame.
Next year the wreath is mine
I rode as far as the last four at [From.Capital.GetName] before I was unhorsed. Not the wreath, but a showing the heralds will remember.
A fair showing
The last pavilion is struck. After days of jousting, feasting and broken bones, the tourney of [Root.Capital.GetName] is over, and the whole land will be talking of it for years.
A tourney worthy of the Lady
The heralds proclaim the champion of my tourney: [tourney_champion.GetTitledName], the last rider left in the saddle.
[tourney_champion.GetSheHeCap] rode well

My [tourney_champion.GetRelation] [tourney_champion.GetTitledFirstName] is the champion of the tourney of [tourney_host.Capital.GetName]! Every herald in the land will cry the name of House [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName].
Glory to House [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName]!
The tourney of [From.Capital.GetName] is over. After so many days of lances, wine and song, the road home seems very quiet.
It was a fine spectacle
As champion of the tourney of [From.Capital.GetName], the honour falls to me to name the Queen of Love and Beauty. Every lady in the stands is watching me, and so is every husband and father.
Who else but my wife?
My betrothed shall have the honour
My lover is my true queen
[tourney_queen_1.GetFirstName], the fairest in the stands
[tourney_queen_2.GetFirstName], daughter of a great house
[tourney_queen_3.GetFirstName], whose kin are here at the tourney
[tourney_queen_4.GetFirstName] will do
No mortal woman. I lay my wreath before the Lady
will be delighted
[From.GetTitledFirstName] [From.GetOnlyDynastyName], the champion of the tourney, has ridden to the stands and laid the wreath of roses in my lap. I am the Queen of Love and Beauty!
How wonderful!
The champion [tourney_champion.GetTitledName] has named [From.GetTitledName] Queen of Love and Beauty. The crowd cheers as she is crowned with roses.
A fine choice
A great honour for our house!
At the feast after the tourney the Queen of Love and Beauty, [From.GetFirstName], keeps looking my way over the rim of her cup. Could it be that she wants more than a wreath from me?
I shall pursue her
will answer your advances
She is not for me
[From.GetTitledFirstName] [From.GetOnlyDynastyName], the champion who named me his queen, has been at my side all evening with sweet words and wine. Now he asks to walk with me in the gardens...
Embrace the passion
will be thrilled
No, thank you
will be disappointed
After much wine and many sweet words, [From.GetFirstName], my Queen of Love and Beauty, is mine. The tourney could not have ended better.
Wonderful!
For all my charm, [From.GetFirstName], my Queen of Love and Beauty, has turned me away. The wreath, it seems, was all she wanted from me.
Her loss
In the practice runs a squire's lance caught me under the arm and I came off hard. Since then, each time I close my visor, my hands shake. The others have seen it.
I am not made for this
In the practice runs I faced a towering Grail Knight and held my seat when everyone was sure I would fall. Something in me has changed. I am afraid of nothing now.
Let them all come!
A night of wine in the pavilion of a fellow knight ended somewhere I never expected, and I find I do not regret it.
Some things are best kept between knights
The camp followers' wagons stand at the edge of every tourney, and I spent more nights there than in my pavilion. Now it burns when I piss and there are sores where no knight wants them.
Curse those wagons!
The ale tents never close during a tourney, and I have hardly left them since I arrived. I wake each morning with a sore head and reach for the cup before my boots.
Another!
Between the jousts the knights fight on foot with blunted swords, and I have done little else all week. An old master-at-arms took an interest in me and taught me tricks I will never forget.
My blade is quicker now
The stands are full of whispers: who sleeps with whom, who owes what to whom, who paid whom to fall. I have listened to all of it, and learned a great deal.
I was caught listening at the wrong pavilion and the whole tourney laughed at me. It will be a long time before anyone trusts me with a secret again.
The merchants who follow the tourney sell everything from horseshoes to holy relics. Haggling with them all week has taught me more about money than my steward ever did.
The merchants of the tourney fair fleeced me shamelessly. A relic of the Lady that turned out to be a pig's knucklebone, a horse that went lame the next day... I do not want to count what I spent.
Every evening of the tourney has been a feast, and every feast a chance to make friends. I have shared cups with half the lords of the land.
At the feast I told a jest about the host's mother that was very funny in my head. Nobody laughed. Nobody has spoken to me since.
A lesson learned
I would rather forget it

A Knight of the Realm who watched me ride has come to my pavilion. He says I ride like one born to the lance and offers to dub me a knight of Bretonnia here and now, before the Lady and the whole tourney.
I kneel. I deserve this
Thank you, but no
For [From.GetHerHis] bold showing in the lists of my tourney, [From.GetTitledName] has been dubbed a Knight Errant before the whole crowd.
A worthy new knight
I stumble out to the lists in a haze of ale, ready for my next tilt. I put my foot in the stirrup, miss, and fall flat on my back in the sand. A thousand people are laughing at me.
By the Lady, what was I thinking...

It is [From.GetBestName]'s turn to ride, but [From.GetSheHe] stumbles out late and drunk as a peasant at harvest, falls off [From.GetHerHis] horse before it has moved and lies giggling in the sand. All eyes turn to me.
Ha! Now there is someone who knows how to celebrate!
This is an outrage! Get [From.GetHerHim] off my field!
[From.GetBestName] laughed until [From.GetSheHe] cried and the crowd laughed with [From.GetHerHim]. Still, I am out of the lists, and the tale of my fall will follow me for a while.
[From.GetBestName] is furious at the insult to [From.GetHerHis] tourney and has had me thrown off the field. Every knight in the land will hear of it.
No glory for me this year

All week a peasant boy of twelve or so has held my horse, polished my armour and run my errands without a word of thanks. Today he fell to his knees in front of me and begged to serve me as a squire. Peasant or not, the boy has a good heart and a strong arm.
Get up, boy. You may serve me
Off with you. Squires are not made from peasants

My squire [tourney_squire.GetFirstName] is supposed to be readying my horse. Instead I find him face down outside the camp followers' wagons, stinking of ale and worse, with no idea where he left my lance.
Oh well. I was young once
A sharp word will sober him
The flat of my sword will sober him faster
Between the jousts I take [tourney_squire.GetFirstName] out to the practice field and drill [tourney_squire.GetHerHim] at the lance, the sword and the saddle until we are both dripping.
Again! From the top!

At the feast [tourney_boaster.GetTitledName] stands up with a cup in [tourney_boaster.GetHerHis] hand and tells the whole hall that [tourney_boaster.GetSheHe] has won more jousts than I have had hot dinners, and that I sit a horse like a sack of turnips. The hall is laughing.
Ha! [tourney_boaster.GetSheHeCap] merely jests
I will show [tourney_boaster.GetHerHim] in the lists
I throw my gauntlet at [tourney_boaster.GetHerHis] feet!
[tourney_boaster.GetFirstName] is challenged to a duel.
will become your rival
My boasting at the feast has not gone down well with [From.GetTitledName], who swore before the whole hall to make me eat my words in the lists.
Let [From.GetHerHim] try!

A woman in white walks among the pavilions at dusk, and the knights fall silent as she passes. She is a Damsel of the Lady, one of those maidens taken by the Fay Enchantress to learn the Lady's secrets. She stops before me, and looks at me for a long time.
I kneel before her and ask the Lady's blessing
I bow and walk on. I need no witch's blessing
